aspects.fertilizer:
General nutrient requirements:
Determine fertilizer quantity per acre based on laboratory soil analysis.
Average fertility soil requires 12 kilograms nitrogen, 12 kilograms phosphorus, and 12 kilograms potash per acre.
Balanced and proportional fertilizer protects the crop from harmful climate change impacts and improves yield.

Fertilizer options at sowing:
Option one is half a bag of DAP and half a bag of SOP.
Option two is one and a quarter bags of SSP 18 percent, 8 kilograms of urea, and half a bag of SOP.
Option three is one third of a bag of Nitrophos, one bag of SSP 18 percent, and half a bag of SOP.

Barani areas:
Apply the entire quantity of fertilizer at sowing time.

Irrigated areas:
Apply all phosphorus, all potash, and one third of nitrogen fertilizer at sowing.
Apply the remaining nitrogen in two equal splits.
Apply the first split of remaining nitrogen with the first irrigation.
Apply the second split of remaining nitrogen before flowering.
Apply 4 to 5 kilograms of sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.

Fertilizer alternatives and micro-nutrients:
Use ammonium sulphate instead of urea if it is available.
Boron application is beneficial for increased flowering and pollination.
MOP can replace SOP if SOP is unavailable, but apply 2 kilograms of sulfur per acre with it.

Private company seeds:
Apply fertilizer at the rates recommended by the private companies when using their seed.

Punjab Soil Fertility Research Institute and app:
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app called Khad Hisab.
Farmers can download Khad Hisab from the Google Play Store.
The app provides balanced fertilizer recommendations for Taramira and other crops with or without a soil test report.
A short introductory video is available in the app description box to guide users.
Contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory for further information.
aspects.harvesting:
**Low-Rainfall and Barani Areas:**
Taramira is cultivated in Bhakkar, Khushab, Rahim Yar Khan, Mianwali, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur districts, and other low-rainfall areas.
Sowing time in barani areas is 1 September to the end of October.
Harvesting time is mid-March or end of March to the beginning of April.

**Irrigated Areas:**
Sowing time is the beginning of October to mid-November.
Harvesting time is mid-March or end of March to the beginning of April.

**Rawalpindi Division:**
Sowing time is mid-August to the end of September.
Harvesting time is the month of March.

**Storage and Insect Management:**
Ensure the produce is thoroughly dry before storing.
Moisture content must not exceed 8 percent.
Grains should make a cracking sound when chewed with teeth.
Excess moisture creates a risk of fungus on the seed.
Keep seeds of different varieties separate during storage.
Inspect warehouses regularly for insect attacks.
Fumigate stores with 30 to 35 tablets of Aluminum Phosphide per 1000 cubic feet to protect against insect attacks.

**Spray Applications and Chemical Disposal:**
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pests.
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.

**Domestic Oil Refining:**
Refining taramira oil domestically produces low-cost, impurity-free, nutrient-rich cooking oil.
Extract crude oil using a kohlu or expeller.
Place 5 kilograms of crude oil in a pot or pan.
Heat the oil to a temperature of 85 degrees Celsius.
Do not let the oil boil, but ensure it is too hot to touch the pot.
Add 150 grams of finely ground Gachni or Fuller's earth into the hot oil.
Stir thoroughly with a spoon for 5 minutes, then remove it from the stove.
Make a triangular bag out of thick market cloth.
Hang the bag from a sturdy stand or charpai and place a clean container underneath.
Pour the lukewarm oil into the cloth bag to filter it.
aspects.irrigation:
Rain-fed areas:
Summer rains are very important for the Taramira crop in rain-fed areas.
Kharif crops benefit directly from summer rains, while Taramira is sown using the preserved soil moisture from these rains.
Methods should be used to absorb summer rainwater into the soil and conserve it for a long time instead of letting it run off as waste.
Properly conserving monsoon rainwater can increase Taramira crop yield by 20 to 25 percent.

Irrigation and water management:
Take special care of irrigation in case of drought.
Sow the crop on ridges to protect it from the effects of excessive rains.
Ridge sowing reduces crop damage and makes it easier to drain excess water from the field.
Stay informed about weather forecasts before sowing the crop or applying irrigation.

Pest management:
Flood 1 liter per acre of Fipronil 5 percent SC with irrigation water to protect Taramira from termite attacks.

Crop care:
Sow the crop at the recommended time.
Pay special attention to plant protection.
aspects.machinery:
**Land preparation and sowing:**
Prepare the land thoroughly.
Use a laser land leveler for land leveling.
Sow the crop in rows at a distance of 1 to 1.5 feet.
Sow in good soil moisture conditions with a row-to-row distance of 1.5 feet.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.
A small seed drill is available for sowing and yields very good results.
Seed depth must not exceed 1 to 1.5 inches.

**Ridge sowing:**
For ridge sowing, broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation.
Run a plow and plank, then make ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor.
A planter named ridger-cum-seeder has been introduced by various companies and is available in the market for this method.

**Spraying equipment and operation:**
Before spraying, check the machine by filling it with plain water and determine the required water volume.
Use the recommended water quantity to ensure uniform spray coverage.
Do not stand against the direction of the wind while spraying.
Do not spray in strong winds.
Avoid repeated use of poisons from the same chemical group.
Use a flat fan nozzle or flood jet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control.

**Pesticide waste disposal:**
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.
aspects.other:
Greens harvesting:
Farmers commonly pick greens from the Taramira crop.
Picking greens increases the risk of aphid attack on the crop.
Picking greens also reduces crop yield.
Allocate a separate area for obtaining greens in a crop cultivated for seed to protect the remaining crop from damage.

Climate change impacts:
Climate change causes harmful effects on Taramira due to unexpected rains, heavy rains, or drought.

Crop management and protection:
Sow the crop at the recommended time to protect Taramira from the effects of climate change.
Ensure proper plant protection.
Stay informed about the weather forecast before sowing or applying irrigation.

High rainfall areas:
Cultivate the crop mandatorily on ridges in high rainfall areas.
aspects.overview:
General Overview:
Taramira is an oilseed crop included in the 2025-26 oilseed production plan to increase domestic edible oil production and reduce costly imports. Its seed contains 30 to 35 percent oil. Green stems and leaves are consumed as greens. Traditional healers recommend it for stomach disorders, acidity, chronic constipation, and joint pain.

Punjab Annual Statistics:
In 2020-21, cultivated area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, cultivated area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), total production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, cultivated area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), total production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, cultivated area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), total production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
In 2024-25, provisional estimates show an area of 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), total production of 499.94 thousand metric tons, and an average yield of 15.23 maunds per acre.

Recommended Variety:
RD-73 is the recommended variety developed by the Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal. It is high yielding, possesses resistance against pests and diseases, and has a yield potential of up to 13 maunds per acre.

Regional Suitability:
Taramira is cultivated in Bhakkar, Khushab, Rahim Yar Khan, Mianwali, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, and other low-rainfall areas. It grows successfully in low-rainfall rain-fed areas and salt-affected soils. In sandy and irrigation-limited soils of Thal and Cholistan, taramira is profitable. In Thal, mixed cropping with gram gives good results.

Crop Calendar:
Rain-fed areas: Sowing is from 1 September to the end of October. Harvesting is from mid-March or late March to early April.
Irrigated areas: Sowing is from early October to mid-November. Harvesting is from mid-March or late March to early April.
Rawalpindi Division: Sowing is from mid-August to the end of September. Harvesting is in March.

Extension and Promotion:
The Agriculture Department publishes the production plan first. Extension staff writes slogans and recommendations on walls, milestones, and signboards. The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension prepares a district strategy, notifies the provincial government, and mobilizes field staff. District and tehsil level training programs are conducted for extension staff and farmers. The Directorate General of Agricultural Information runs promotional campaigns via print, electronic, and social media.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Management:
Taramira resists diseases, insects, and shattering. Harvesting saag increases aphid attacks and lowers yield, so reserve a separate area for saag. Treat seed with fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram seed. For stem rot, treat seed with 1 gram Thiophanate-methyl per kilogram seed. Rotate crops and destroy infected residues.

Irrigated Termite Control:
Insects damage underground parts during dry weather. Apply recommended pesticide at rauni, or flood 1 liter Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre with irrigation water.

Rain-fed Barani Termite Control:
Mix recommended pesticide into 15 to 20 kilograms of fine soil, broadcast before sowing, and plow.

Grasshopper:
Attacks emerging seedlings, especially near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum. Spray per acre 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Mustard Sawfly:
Larvae damage leaves in October and November. Per acre spray: 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 milliliters Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams Fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug:
Bugs measuring 5 to 7 millimeters suck sap in October and November. Per acre spray: 400 milliliters Abamectin + Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams Acephate 75 SP, or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Larvae eat leaf edges in patches. Per acre spray: 80 milliliters Chlorantraniliprole + Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 milliliters Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Aphids:
Pests suck sap from mid-January to late March. Complete sowing by the first week of October. Per acre spray: 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 milliliters Clothianidin 20 EC.

Punjab Biological Control:
Chrysoperla cards are provided free by Punjab Agriculture Extension laboratories in Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Foliar Disease Management:
For white rust, spray Propiconazole or Difenoconazole at 1.25 milliliters per liter water.
For epidemic blight during rains at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius, spray Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 2.5 milliliters per liter water.
For downy mildew, spray Flumorph + Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams or Mancozeb + Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter water.
For bacterial stem rot, spray Benzothiazolinone at 2.5 milliliters, Streptomycin sulphate at 1 gram, or Kasugamycin at 6 milliliters per liter water.
For stem rot, spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 2.5 milliliters per liter water.
For seedling blight, spray Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram or Metiram + Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter water.
For rust, spray Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram or Propiconazole at 2 milliliters per liter water.

Application Safety:
Spray at economic thresholds during the evening to protect pollinators, ladybird beetles, and syrphid flies. Use hollow cone nozzles for insects and flat fan or floodjet nozzles for weeds. Avoid hoeing immediately after spraying. Wear protective equipment and bury empty containers.
aspects.sowing:
Suitable Regions:
Taramira is cultivated in Bhakkar, Khushab, Rahim Yar Khan, Mianwali, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, and other low rainfall areas.
It is profitable in sandy soils with limited irrigation in Thal and Cholistan.
In Thal, mixed cropping with gram gives good results.

Sowing and Harvesting Dates:
Barani areas sowing time is September 1 to the end of October.
Barani areas harvesting time is mid March or end of March to early April.
Irrigated areas sowing time is start of October to mid November.
Irrigated areas harvesting time is mid March or end of March to early April.
Rawalpindi Division sowing time is mid August to the end of September.
Rawalpindi Division harvesting time is the month of March.

Barani Land Preparation:
Conserve monsoon moisture by plowing deeply in empty fields before the rains.
Strengthen field bunds, level the land, and plow across the slope.
Do not plow after the monsoon season.
Before sowing, plow twice and plank to conserve moisture.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.
The field must be weed free and leveled with a laser land leveler.

Sowing Methods and Spacing:
Sow in moist soil conditions.
Row distance must be 1 to 1.5 feet.
A small seed drill gives good results.
Seed depth must not exceed 1 to 1.5 inches.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.
For ridge sowing, broadcast seed and fertilizer, run a plow and plank, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger cum seeder planter is available for ridge sowing.
Ridge sowing protects the crop from heavy rains and helps drain excess water.

Thinning:
Thinning is essential and must be completed before the first irrigation.
Thin when the crop has 4 leaves.
Remove weak and diseased plants during thinning.
Maintain plant to plant distance of 9 to 12 inches.

Weed Control:
Spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing when temperatures are 35 degrees Celsius or lower.
For drill and moist soil sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.

Crop Care:
Ensure timely irrigation during drought.
Check weather forecasts before sowing and before irrigating.
aspects.varieties:
**Recommended Variety and Yield:**
The approved Taramira variety is RD-73, developed by the Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal.
It has high yield potential of up to 13 maunds per acre.
It is resistant to insects and diseases.

**Seed Sources:**
Limited seed is available from Punjab Seed Corporation, National Agricultural Research Centre Islamabad, Taramira Section at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad, Taramira Research Centre Khanpur, Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur, and Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal.
Seed is also available from registered private seed companies.
Farmers should only use seed certified by the Federal Seed Certification Department.

**Field Preparation and Sowing:**
Prepare the soil thoroughly and level it with a laser leveler.
Sowing depth must not exceed 1.5 inches.
Optimal soil moisture is required for proper germination.
Use clean, healthy seed with a germination rate of at least 80 percent.

**Seed Rates:**
Irrigated areas require 1.5 to 2 kg seed per acre.
Rain-fed (barani) areas require 1.5 to 2 kg per acre, or 2 to 2.5 kg per acre.
Cholistan requires 3 to 4 kg seed per acre.

**Seed Treatment:**
Apply recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg of seed.
Do not increase the fungicide dose and maintain suitable water quantity to avoid damaging seed germination.
If these precautions cannot be taken, do not apply fungicide.
To prevent stem rot, treat seed at sowing with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg of seed.

**Downy Mildew Control:**
Use healthy seed and destroy crop residues.
When symptoms appear, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter of water.
Alternatively, spray Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water.

**Stem Rot Control:**
If stem rot appears on the crop, spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

**Wilt Control:**
Wilt causes seeds to rot, plants to wither and dry, and root bark to crack.
To control wilt, treat seed with recommended fungicide, avoid early sowing, eradicate weeds, and rotate crops.
aspects.weeds:
### Barani Areas:
Deep plough empty fields before monsoon rains to conserve moisture.
Strengthen field borders, level the ground, and plough across the slope.
Do not plough after the monsoon season.
Plough twice and apply planking before sowing to prevent moisture loss.
Ensure the field is level and weed-free at sowing time.
Prepare land in the evening or in the morning before sunrise.

### Common Weeds:
Common weeds found in Taramira include wild oat, dumbi sitti, lashkni booti, bathu, karand, shahtra, and it sit.

### Non-Chemical Weed Control:
For the dab method, plough and apply heavy planking after pre-sowing irrigation or rain when soil is in wattar condition.
Leave the field for 5 to 7 days to let weeds germinate, then destroy them during seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain.
Perform the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Perform the second hoeing after irrigation when the soil reaches wattar condition.
Thin the crop when it reaches the 4-leaf stage to maintain recommended plant spacing.

### Chemical Weed Control:
Spray recommended Pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre before emergence.
When temperature is 35 degrees Celsius or below, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill and wattar sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
To control it sit within 2 weeks of crop emergence, spray 400 to 500 ml Metazachlor 50 percent SC per acre.
Metazachlor spray can be applied without a protective shield.

### Spray Equipment and Safety:
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect sprays.
Bury empty chemical bottles in the soil and destroy cardboard boxes.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after herbicide spraying.
Immediate hoeing breaks the chemical barrier, allows weeds to regrow, and exposes the farmer to toxic dust.

### Wilt Disease Management:
Wilt causes rotting seeds, withered dry plants, and cracked root bark.
Treat seeds with recommended fungicides before sowing.
Avoid early sowing, destroy weeds, and rotate crops to control wilt.
